LHX.sentence: L3Harris has edged up a touch and sits well below its highs for the year — profit margins are running leaner than usual, but it's still the smallest of the big defense contractors and steady military spending keeps the business intact.

ASML.sentence: ASML drifted down slightly; it looks eye-wateringly expensive on the surface, but that's mostly because its earnings are in a temporary dip right now, not because the business has changed — they're still the only company making the machines that print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde had a quiet, slightly down week — the industrial gas business just hums along on long-term contracts and small price increases, and there's no real story here right now.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — their Azure cloud is still growing fast off the back of AI demand, and the whole story keeps grinding along without any drama ahead of their next earnings update.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher ticked up, and there's a quietly encouraging sign underneath: biotech funding is thawing again, which usually means more lab-equipment orders for them a few quarters down the line.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge rose a touch and pays a healthy dividend — this is the toll-road of oil and gas pipelines, chugging along as it always does.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow had a good day as big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its workflow and AI-assistant tools, and those future contracts are still growing at a solid clip.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped a few percent even as copper prices have been surging — the miner is lagging behind the metal it digs up, which sometimes sets up a catch-up later.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta drifted up, and the key thing is the price it charges for a ton of rock is still climbing nicely — a recent dip in the headline price figure is just a mix quirk, not real weakness, though its earnings look flattered by a one-off gain so don't mistake it for cheap.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA slipped slightly, mostly because the Mexican peso has been weakening — and since much of its earnings are in pesos, that's a drag when converted back to dollars.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is steady and pays a very generous dividend, and with oil prices well above the level it needs to break even, there's plenty of cash cushion behind that payout.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, barely moved — notably, its shares are priced below what it would cost to simply replace its fleet of ships, so the market is valuing it quite cheaply.

MA.sentence: Mastercard ticked up and is priced right in line with rival Visa, even though it usually commands a small premium — meanwhile people keep tapping their cards more and more, so the toll keeps rolling in.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company rose a touch; even after a strong recovery off its low, it's trading well below its own typical valuation, which is unusual for a business that keeps selling more supplies with every operation.
